preamble: A bilabial [b] becomes the velar [g] almost only before the labio-velar glide [w], or a rounded vowel. There the glide's velar constriction takes over as the primary place and the lips stay involved through the rounding. In the Central Volta-Comoe (Akan) languages, morph-initial *b that had become labialized [bʷ] changed to [gʷ], while Eastern and Western Volta-Comoe kept [b]. Rural and popular Spanish shows the same [bw] > [gw] in güeno for bueno and agüelo for abuelo.

examples.from: Early Volta-Comoe *b- 'sheep' (cf. Larteh bwui, Nzema bwuani)
examples.note: Before the shift, labialization produced [bʷ]; Asante, Akyem and Kwawu went on to front [gʷ] to [ɟɥ] (ɟɥan).

examples.from: Early Volta-Comoe *b- 'market' (cf. Larteh bji, Nzema bjia)

examples.note: The from form is the standard pronunciation, which keeps the conservative [bw].
An eye-dialect spelling of the popular pronunciation; the form was also borrowed into Catalan.
